prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1406; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in at an intersection in Conroe, Texas. Is it all right if we proceed?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just be referred to as the claimant for this, if that works.

Q: That's acceptable. Can you describe what you were doing just before the collision?

A: I was stopped at a red light in the right-hand lane, waiting to turn. The traffic had been moving slowly all morning.

Q: What happened next?

A: The vehicle behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind and my head snapped back and forward.

Q: Did you notice any injuries at the scene?

A: Not right away. I felt stiff, but I thought I'd just be sore for a day or two. By that evening my neck was tight and my lower back was aching.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next day. They diagnosed a neck and back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a referral to a physical therapist.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. Turning my head to check mirrors is painful, and I can't sit for long periods without my back complaining. I've had to take time off from some of my usual work.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm following my treatment plan and I want to get back to normal as soon as I can.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the recorded statement.
